items.title: The induced transformation on a symmetric subinterval satisfies the same conjugacy equation
items.author: Przemyslaw Berk; Frank Trujillo
items.work: Ergodic properties of infinite extension of symmetric interval exchange transformations
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 626-628: the transformation induced by a symmetric interval exchange transformation on a symmetric subinterval again satisfies the conjugacy equation between the reflection and the inverse. The proof (source lines 630-646) has to relate the return time to the subinterval with the return time to itself along the orbit, and the identification of the two inverse iterates is justified not by computation but by the local reflection lemma, which says that an iterate of a point lies in the subinterval exactly when its conjugate does; a second case, where the subinterval is symmetric about the middle of the whole interval rather than about a continuity interval, is then treated separately. The statement records the conjugacy equation and neither the return-time comparison nor the case distinction.
